 34     I.     Introduction

35     Southern Skye Ranch opposes selection of routes utilizing the P41/P42/M8 crossing affecting
36     its property because the admitted evidence demonstrates that significant site-specific
37     floodplain, erosion, access, and river-corridor conditions were not fully evaluated before route
38     selection, while multiple feasible route alternatives remain available for Commission
39     consideration.
40
41   Il.     Relevant Hearing Evidence
42
43   A. The Record Demonstrates That Significant Site-Specific Conditions Exist At the
44   Southern Skye Ranch Crossing and Were Not Fully Evaluated Before Route Selection.
45
46   Ryan Smith testified that the portions of Southern Skye Ranch affected by proposed Route P41
47   are located within an active floodplain and riparian environment associated with the San Saba
48   River. He further testified that he personally observed multiple significant flooding events during
49   2025 that caused erosion, vegetation loss, tree loss, access limitations, and significant
50   floodwater movement throughout the proposed crossing area. 1
51
52   Mr. Smith also testified that portions of the ranch bottomland became inaccessible during major
53   flood events and that those access limitations directly affect the operational feasibility of
54   maintaining infrastructure within the proposed crossing area. 2
55
56   The admitted photographic evidence demonstrates significant flooding and erosion impacts
57   within the proposed crossing area. 3
58
59   During cross-examination, Applicant witness Russell Marusak testified that no boots-on-the-
60   ground field assessments had been conducted at the proposed P41 crossing location after the
61   July 2025 flood events and before route selection.4
62
63   Mr. Marusak further testified that the July 2025 flooding events were not evaluated at the specific
64   Southern Skye Ranch crossing location as part of the environmental assessment and route
65   evaluation process. 5
66
67   When asked whether any analysis of those flood events had been documented for the Southern
68   Skye Ranch crossing, Mr. Marusak testified: "For the ranch at that crossing, no." 6
69
70   Accordingly the record demonstrates that significant site-specific floodplain, erosion, access,
71   and river-corridor conditions existed at the Southern Skye Ranch crossing location, but that
72   detailed post-flood field investigation of those conditions did not occur before route selection.

82    B. Multiple Feasible Route Alternatives Remain Available for Commission Consideration.
83
84
85    Applicant witness Brenda Perkins testified that all 122 filed routes had been reviewed from an
86    engineering and constructability standpoint and deemed acceptable from an engineering
87    perspective. 7
88
89    Ms. Perkins further acknowledged that the route ultimately recommended by the Applicants is
90    not the only feasible route available for Commission consideration. 8
91
92    The hearing record further demonstrates that additional route alternatives were developed after
93    public input and that route links were modified following the public meeting process. 9
94
95    These admissions demonstrate that multiple feasible route alternatives remain available for
96    Commission consideration. Accordingly, the record demonstrates both that multiple feasible
97    alternatives remain available and that route development was not fixed or incapable of further
98    refinement once site-specific concerns became known.
 99

107    Ill.      Argument
108
109    The hearing record demonstrates that significant site-specific floodplain, erosion, access, and
110    river-corridor conditions exist at the Southern Skye Ranch crossing location. The record further
111    demonstrates that these conditions were not evaluated through post-flood field assessment
112    before route selection.
113



                                                              3
 114   The hearing record also demonstrates that multiple feasible route alternatives remain available
115   for Commission consideration. Applicant witnesses confirmed that multiple filed routes are
116   feasible, that the Applicants' recommended route is not the only feasible route available for
117   Commission consideration, and that route development continued to evolve throughout the
118   routing process.
119
120   The hearing record further demonstrates that route selection involves balancing competing
121   routing factors and professional judgment rather than reliance on any single metric.
122
123   Accordingly the Commission should give meaningful weight to the site-specific floodplain,
124   erosion, access, and river-corridor impacts established in the Southern Skye Ranch evidence
125   when selecting a final route.
126
127
128
129   IV.    Requested Findings of Fact
130
131   Finding of Fact No. 1
132   The Southern Skye Ranch crossing experienced significant flooding, erosion, and access
133   limitations during the July 2025 flood events.
134
135   Finding of Fact No. 2
136   Applicants did not conduct boots-on-the-ground surveys of the proposed P41 crossing location
137   after the July 2025 flood events and before route selection.
138
139   Finding of Fact No. 3
140   Multiple feasible route alternatives remain available for Commission consideration.
141
142   Finding of Fact No. 4
143   Alternative route concepts were developed, and route modifications occurred during route
144   development.
145
146   Finding of Fact No. 5
147   Route selection involves balancing competing routing factors and professional judgment rather
148   than purely mathematical scoring.
149

 V.     Conclusion

Accordingly the Commission should avoid selecting a route utilizing the Southern Skye Ranch
crossing where multiple feasible alternatives remain available and where the record
demonstrates significant site-specific floodplain, erosion, access, and river-corridor impacts that
were not fully evaluated before route selection.




Respectfully submitted,
